rationale: X independently catches the ground-truth-confirmed Skip-Softmax timestep bug (denoise_loop.py:210, correctly proposing the t=1-sigma fix that the human 'Readiness fixes' comment confirms was pushed), and touches both the AllGather-KV (layer.py:96) and duplicate-boundary/SAGE (trtllm_attn.py:305) code regions the two inline ground-truth comments concern, albeit shallowly (framed as test gaps rather than diagnosed bugs). Y gives a technically sharper, more deeply verified review (concrete reproduction snippets for unvalidated max_seqlen and zero-token mask, device-sync count) but explicitly asserts it 'verified the convention is right' on the timestep issue — directly contradicting the ground-truth fix — and never addresses the aligned-packed/SAGE duplicate-terminal-boundary concern at all. Both are well-grounded and highly actionable; X's edge comes from better alignment with the actual reviewer concerns, while Y's extra findings, though valid and precise, mostly fall outside the ground-truth set and include one confident wrong claim.
